payload.result:
Dataset: Columbia University publications, 2021-2024 (OpenAlex snapshot of 2026-11-23)
Works (papers, preprints, books, datasets, ...) published 2021-2024 with at least one author affiliated with Columbia University (OpenAlex institution I78577930 and its OpenAlex child institutions: NASA GISS, Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, ICAP, CZ Biohub NY), taken from the OpenAlex API on 2026-11-23 and never refreshed. Includes all co-authors and their institutions, the OpenAlex topic hierarchy, profiles of Columbia-affiliated authors, venues, outgoing references, yearly citation counts, keywords and funders.

Tables:
- authors (29,518 rows): Profiles of authors who are Columbia-affiliated on at least one snapshot work.
- authorship_institutions (619,528 rows): Institutions listed by each author on each work (an author can list se
... [1,841 characters truncated] ...
 had less time to be cited.
- citations lists every outgoing reference; only rows with cited_in_snapshot = true point to works that are themselves in this dataset (and therefore have metadata here).
- authors contains profiles only for authors who are Columbia-affiliated on at least one work in the snapshot; other co-authors appear only in authorships (name and id).
- Profile metrics in authors and sources (works_count, cited_by_count, h_index, ...) are global OpenAlex values for the whole career / whole venue, not restricted to this snapshot.
- Some works have no abstract (abstract is NULL), no topic, or no source.

Counting rules:
- authorships has one row per (work, author); count works with count(DISTINCT work_id) after joining it.
- authorships.is_columbia is true when that author lists a Columbia institution on that specific work.
- A work can have up to 3 topics in work_topics; works.primary_topic_* gives the single primary one.
- work_topics joins to topics for the full hierarchy domain > field > subfield > topic.

Relationships:
- works.work_id = authorships.work_id
- authorships.(work_id, author_order) = authorship_institutions.(work_id, author_order)
- authorship_institutions.institution_id = institutions.institution_id
- authorships.author_id = authors.author_id
- works.source_id = sources.source_id
- works.primary_topic_id = topics.topic_id
- work_topics.work_id = works.work_id ; work_topics.topic_id = topics.topic_id
- citations.citing_work_id = works.work_id
- citations.cited_work_id = works.work_id
- work_citations_by_year.work_id = works.work_id
- work_keywords.work_id = works.work_id
- work_funders.work_id = works.work_id

payload.text:
Columbia’s publication output **rebounded in 2024 but remained 1.6% below 2021**. The snapshot counts went from **14,175** works in 2021 to **13,636** in 2022 and **13,616** in 2023, before rising to **13,944** in 2024. [T1, F1]

Among the eight largest fields, **Computer Science grew the most** (+22.2%), driven by a jump from 786 works in 2023 to 979 in 2024. **Environmental Science fell every year** (−11.4%), while **Medicine remained by far the largest field** and ended just 2.0% below 2021. [T2]

| Field, ranked by four-year output | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2024 vs. 2021 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Medicine | 4,005 | 3,906 | 3,914 | 3,925 | −2.0% |
| Social Sciences | 1,676 | 1,598 | 1,557 | 1,608 | −4.1% |
| Computer Science | 801 | 803 | 786 | 979 | +22.2% |
| Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology | 777 | 795 | 811 | 769 | −1.0% |
| Psychology | 763 | 741 | 700 | 739 | −3.1% |
| Environmental Science | 769 | 731 | 683 | 681 | −11.4% |
| Physics and Astronomy | 567 | 594 | 689 | 668 | +17.8% |
| Neuroscience | 560 | 538 | 635 | 595 | +6.3% |

Source: [T2]. In the [interactive view](view1), hover over a field for its four-year total and net change. You can adjust how many fields are shown and switch the trend lines between work counts and percentage change relative to 2021.

**Scope:** Each OpenAlex work counts once, under its primary field, and “publication output” includes all work types in the snapshot, not just journal articles. Works without a primary field count toward the overall totals but not the field rankings. The snapshot excludes works with more than 100 authors and works affiliated only with separately indexed institutions such as Columbia University Irving Medical Center. [T1, T2]

Two useful follow-ups: Was the Computer Science jump driven by articles, conference papers, or preprints? Which Environmental Science subfields accounted for the decline?
